collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a teen aged 16-17 and an adult)

collection.description: A teen wants a hut of their own, right now: help build it, or ask them to wait a year.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) wants a hut of (subject.his/her) own. Not later. Now. (subject.He/she) has picked a spot, sketched the walls in the sand, and worked out how many poles (subject.he/she) needs. (subject.He/she) explains all of this to (friend) at great length, while (friend) is trying to eat breakfast.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Next year," says (friend). "When you're grown." (subject) argues. (friend) listens, and doesn't budge, but agrees that (subject) can start gathering poles now. All year (subject) gathers poles. By the time (subject.he/she) is allowed to build, (subject.he/she) has enough for two huts. Nobody has the heart to point this out.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "Alright," says (friend). "But you do the work, I just hold things." It takes most of a season. The roof leaks the first time it rains, and (subject) fixes it (subject.him/her)self, muttering. The first night (subject.he/she) sleeps there, (subject.he/she) is back at the family fire for breakfast. And dinner. And most lunches. But (subject.he/she) sleeps in (subject.his/her) own hut.
